prompt: My frontend pod is in CrashLoopBackOff. What should I check first?
expected: The agent should load references/debug.md and/or references/commands.md and provide kubectl triage commands like `kubectl describe pod` and `kubectl logs --previous`.
actual: I will check the pod's status to diagnose the CrashLoopBackOff. I recommend running `kubectl describe pod <frontend-pod-name>` to look at the Events section for readiness/liveness probe failures, and `kubectl logs <frontend-pod-name> --previous` to see the exit reason of the last crashed container.

prompt: We are experiencing random 502 Bad Gateway errors on our new ingress. The deployment seems fine.
expected: The agent should load references/ingress.md and/or references/networking.md, checking Service endpoints/EndpointSlices and Ingress controller timeout/protocol mismatches.
actual: Random 502 errors often indicate the Ingress cannot reach the backend Service endpoints. Let's verify EndpointSlices map correctly to the running pods with `kubectl get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=<service-name>`. I will also load references/ingress.md to check whether the controller timeout or backend protocol matches the application.

prompt: Our HPA shows <unknown> and never scales even though CPU is high.
expected: The agent should load references/autoscaling.md and/or references/resources.md, explain that utilization needs container requests, and check metrics-server.
actual: HPA utilization is usage divided by requests, so a missing CPU request makes the target show <unknown>. I will confirm every container has requests, then check metrics-server health via references/autoscaling.md before changing the HPA target.
